fact: The World Bank reports 4.4 million households had received at least one tranche of the federal government cash transfer paid directly into bank accounts, and 0.8 million a second, as of 8 October 2024.
The World Bank says payments to recipients' bank accounts are made after validating individuals through the NIN or BVN, and low NIN/BVN coverage among the poor slowed the rollout.

The Central Bank of Nigeria pays Conditional Cash Transfer beneficiaries directly, with bulk payments to five million households due to begin the week after the article and verified households already receiving payment alerts, says the minister's media aide.
Beneficiaries are matched on NIN and BVN with in-person verification and biometrics, and those without a NIN and BVN are disqualified, says the minister's media aide.
NSIPA lists digital payments via bank accounts and wallets, with payment duration cut from 6 months to 3.

Finance minister Wale Edun said the government has disbursed N330 billion as conditional cash transfers to 8.5 million poor households through NASSCO, paid digitally by direct debit to bank accounts or mobile wallets.

The finance minister said beneficiaries are verified through their National Identity Number and payments are linked to NIN-to-account linking, and NASSCO's coordinator said disbursements are tied to NIN for integrity.

The Federal Government's National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention pays selected beneficiaries N50,000 into a mobile wallet, with disbursement announced as started by the humanitarian affairs minister on 30 October 2026 and payments continuing in phases.
system: National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI)

fact: The ministry's NERSI website says beneficiaries are selected from verified national identity records and the National Social Register, enrolment in both is a prerequisite, and the NIN is linked to the mobile wallet that receives the payment.
